additions.sentence: Call 999 or go to A&E for sudden chest pain, severe difficulty breathing or coughing up blood, and ask someone to take you or call an ambulance rather than driving yourself.
additions.evidence: NHS flu page: call 999 or go to A&E for these; ask someone to drive you or call 999; do not drive yourself.

additions.sentence: People aged 65 or over, people who are pregnant, and people with a long-term condition or a weakened immune system should get an urgent GP appointment or contact NHS 111 if they have flu symptoms.
additions.evidence: NHS flu page lists these groups for urgent GP appointment or NHS 111.

additions.sentence: Flu symptoms can include a sudden high temperature, an aching body and feeling exhausted.
additions.evidence: NHS flu page: sudden high temperature, aching body, exhaustion.

additions.sentence: A cold usually causes a runny or blocked nose, sneezing, watery eyes and a sore throat, and does not usually bring a fever or body aches.
additions.evidence: UKHSA: cold usually runny nose, sneezing, watery eyes, throat irritation; usually no fever or body aches.

additions.sentence: Viruses such as RSV, adenovirus and the one that causes COVID-19 can cause cold-like symptoms too.
additions.evidence: UKHSA: RSV, adenovirus, hMPV and COVID-19 can produce similar symptoms.

additions.sentence: The only way to know for sure whether you have flu or COVID-19 is to take a test.
additions.evidence: UKHSA: only a test can confirm flu or COVID-19.

additions.sentence: A pharmacist can recommend suitable cold medicines and check which ones are safe for you, and some are not suitable for children, pregnant women or people taking certain other medicines.
additions.evidence: Common cold NHS page: pharmacist can recommend suitable medicines; some not suitable for children, babies, pregnant women, people on certain medicines.

additions.sentence: The NHS offers the flu vaccine every year, in autumn or winter, to people at higher risk of becoming seriously ill from flu.
additions.evidence: Flu vaccine - NHS: offered every year in autumn or winter to people at higher risk of getting seriously ill from flu.
